That doc explicitly states RTLD_GLOBAL load order determines which of several same-named-symbol copies wins, and numbox already implements a detect-and-refuse guard for exactly this class of problem for sqlite (pysqlite_bridge.py libraries_coordinated()/extract_connection_ptr), confirming the risk pattern is real and recognized in the sibling codebase, but no analogous guard exists in numbduck/utils.py for duckdb. The narrow, correctly-identified gap is a wheel that exports partial C API (some duckdb_* symbols) while still missing duckdb_open specifically (the only probe used) -- that wheel would fail the gate, trigger the standalone fallback, and its early-loaded overlapping symbols would silently win at JIT-resolution time over the standalone's copies, per the load-order mechanism above. This is forward-looking but not idle speculation: numbduck/CLAUDE.md's own Project Status section records that duckdb/duckdb-python#404 has a maintainer committing to add C API export before 1.5.3, and the project's pin (duckdb>=1.3.2,<1.6) does not exclude such an incremental/partial release.
